tier_reason: First-party campaign by the SCS author (harness bodono/solver_benchmarks, raw per-problem results and tables in bodono/solver_benchmarks_results/scs33_2026-09) whose numbers match docs/src/benchmarks/index.rst exactly; hardware is given only as AMD EPYC Zen 3 'Milan' hosts with the exact CPU model string masked, and all solvers are prebuilt PyPI wheels with no compiler or flags stated, so not A, and no independent or peer-reviewed run, so not B.

corrections.baseline: Clarabel 0.11.1 (interior point); the same page also times HiGHS 1.15.1, PIQP 0.6.4, OR-Tools PDLP 9.15, OSQP 1.1.3, ProxQP 0.7.3 and NVIDIA cuOpt 26.8.0 (PIQP and ProxSuite are already listed in wave 8). SuiteSparse (the guessed baseline) is not a baseline here: SCS vendors AMD from SuiteSparse (BSD-3-Clause) and QDLDL from the OSQP project (Apache-2.0) in linsys/external.
corrections.claimed_speedup: Mittelmann LP set, shifted geometric mean time (verified solves of 37): SCS GPU cuDSS 208 s (28), SCS CPU MKL Pardiso 431 s (24), PDLP 733 s (19), Clarabel 817 s (20), PIQP 1352 s (12), cuOpt 2086 s (7), HiGHS 2889 s (9); about 3.9x faster than Clarabel on GPU and 1.9x on CPU (derived from page data), but SCS CPU used MKL Pardiso with 4 threads while Clarabel, PIQP, OSQP, HiGHS and PDLP ran single-threaded at their defaults, and the GPU row is an A100 against 4-core CPU runs. Largest QP quartile at 1e-4: SCS GPU 9.4 s (38 solved), SCS CPU 12.8 s (38), Clarabel 12.6 s (37), PIQP 18.3 s (34), OSQP 29.4 s (32), so SCS CPU is level with Clarabel there, not faster. Page text: 'SCS with cuDSS solves more instances than any other solver, in less than half the geometric mean time of the runner-up.'
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated; every solver was the prebuilt PyPI wheel of its latest September 2026 release (SCS 3.3.1 wheel with MKL Pardiso; cuDSS backend on GPU).
corrections.hardware: CPU runs: Modal containers reserving 4 physical cores (the container sees 20; OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 pinned) on AMD EPYC Zen 3 'Milan' hosts (CPU family 25 model 1, exact model string masked by gVisor; AVX2/FMA, no AVX-512, observed 1.8-3.1 GHz), 16 GB memory (64 GB for the Mittelmann, SDP and large shards); GPU runs: NVIDIA A100-80GB with 8 reserved host cores and 64 GB. Source: bodono/solver_benchmarks_results scs33_2026-09/MANIFEST.md (the SCS page itself says only '4-core Linux x86-64 containers (Modal)').
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark of SCS 3.3.1 by the SCS author on his own harness (bodono/solver_benchmarks branch scs33-campaign commit 24ac4ca, with harness fixes made during the campaign), run 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-18, results in bodono/solver_benchmarks_results campaign scs33_2026-09 (0 stars, no license file), published via cvxgrp/scs PRs #476 and #482; the full raw archive is said to be a release asset but the results repo's Releases section shows none. CPU model only at family level (EPYC Milan, SKU masked) and no compiler flags (prebuilt PyPI wheels), so tier C and not A. Thread counts differ: SCS CPU used MKL Pardiso with OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 while Clarabel, PIQP, OSQP, HiGHS and PDLP ran single-threaded at defaults (stated only in the results MANIFEST, not on the SCS page), and the GPU rows compare an A100 against 4-core CPU runs. The same campaign ran the author's other solver QTQP (and qpo3), which the SCS page omits: on the Mittelmann set QTQP GPU cuDSS has 192 s geometric mean with 27 verified solves against SCS GPU 208 s with 28, and QTQP also beats SCS on all QPs and the largest LP quartile (tables/records_geomean_summary_1e-4.csv), so 'less than half the geometric mean time of the runner-up' holds only among the solvers shown. SCS is not fastest overall: on all 349 LPs HiGHS has shifted geometric mean 5.0 s against 11.9 s for SCS CPU; on all 157 QPs Clarabel is 3.1 s and PIQP 3.7 s against 7.5 s for SCS CPU; on SDPs SCS is last in geometric mean (107.5 s against SDPA 38.2 s) though it solves the most (77 of 94). Each solver is shown from the run whose achieved accuracy is nearest the 1e-4 target (SCS at 1e-4, interior-point codes at 1e-6, or 1e-8 for Clarabel on SDP); the Mittelmann set ran with 1800 s limits on 4 cores, so simplex and interior-point codes time out far more than in Mittelmann's own multi-hour runs ('not a re-run of his benchmark'); failures are charged 3x the time limit (5400 s on the Mittelmann set) in the geometric mean. SCS returned false certificates on QGROW7, QGROW22 and neos-4413714-turia (counted as failures). cuOpt's PDLP mostly fails the independent residual check (7 of 37 pass). Vendored AMD (BSD-3-Clause, SuiteSparse) and QDLDL (Apache-2.0, OSQP project) are OSI-licensed, so the whole tree is copyable.

notes: Every number in the record matches the SCS benchmarks page and the raw tables in bodono/solver_benchmarks_results; metadata (MIT, 638 stars, last commit 2026-10-06 on master, SCS 3.3.1 on PyPI 2026-09-05) checks out. Shortcomings to record: first-party campaign by the SCS author, 4-thread MKL Pardiso SCS against single-threaded Clarabel/PIQP/OSQP/HiGHS/PDLP and A100 GPU against 4-core CPU, the author's own QTQP (faster than SCS GPU on the Mittelmann set, 192 s vs 208 s) omitted from the page, SCS CPU level with Clarabel on the largest QPs and behind HiGHS/Clarabel/PIQP on the full LP and QP sets and last on SDPs, no compiler flags and CPU SKU masked.
